Advances: ancora.parsing

Severity: High (calibrated). Consolidated findings F4 and F23.

F4 — Ancora.Parser stores a raw string-keyed YAML map under "meta" when Zoi rejects the block (lib/ancora/parser.ex:85), but gate.ex:415, status.ex:160, review.ex:335 and change_analysis.ex:46 all read it with atom keys. Verified by running it: a spec-meta block missing one required field makes mix spec.check die with FunctionClauseError in Compare.compare/4, and spec.status, spec.next and spec.prime die with KeyError. Five of eight tasks crash. Only spec.validate survives, because Verifier/AppendOnly/Overlap read through a bilingual accessor. It fails closed, but the primary command hands a stack trace to a user who made exactly the mistake the tool exists to catch, and the correct finding it computed never surfaces.
Fix: store nil on schema-validation failure so the existing nil handling takes over, add one Ancora.Index.subject_id/1, route the four call sites through it, and filter non-binary ids before they reach Compare.compare/4. Add a regression test running every corpus-reading task against a spec whose spec-meta is missing a required field.

F23 — the same root cause produces four byte-identical copies of a String.to_existing_atom-in-a-rescue key accessor (parser.ex:234, verifier.ex:353, append_only.ex:147, overlap.ex:166, plus a fifth variant at review/html.ex:300). Exceptions as control flow in a hot accessor. Fix: move the accessor into Ancora.Index as one function built on a compile-time key map, drop the rescue, delete the copies. Note the string-keyed OUTER index shape is a deliberate semver commitment (ancora.parsing.stable_public_api) and must not change; the heterogeneous type under "meta" is the defect.

Lands with F4 as one change.

Verification:
- Tests to pass: a new regression test (test/ancora/index_test.exs or test/mix/tasks/*_test.exs) running spec.check, spec.status, spec.next, spec.prime, spec.review, and spec.validate against a corpus whose spec-meta block is missing one required field, asserting a finding line and a verdict and no crash; tagged tests under ancora.parsing (test/ancora/parser_test.exs, test/ancora/verifier_test.exs, test/ancora/append_only_test.exs, test/ancora/overlap_test.exs)
- Behaviors to demonstrate: (1) Parser stores nil under "meta" on schema failure and every reader tolerates nil; (2) one Ancora.Index.subject_id/1 (or equivalent) replaces the four atom-key reads at gate.ex, status.ex, review.ex, change_analysis.ex; (3) one compile-time key accessor in Ancora.Index replaces the four rescue-based copies plus the html.ex variant, no rescue left; (4) Compare.compare/4 never receives a non-binary id; (5) the string-keyed OUTER index shape is byte-for-byte unchanged (stable_public_api)
- Verification cadence:
  - Iteration tier: mix test --stale or explicitly named test files, plus mix spec.validate; no full suite mid-iteration.
  - Final tier: immediately before IMPLEMENTED, run-until-green: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission
  - Verifier tier: mix spec.check --base the epic base sha recorded at admission plus tagged and --stale selections only; do NOT run the full suite.
- Standing bounce-class checks:
  - Production call site named for each new callable surface, with the proving test that exercises that production path.
  - Fixture hygiene: one TmpGitRepo per test, no shared temp dirs, async only where the fixture allows.
  - Spec surfaces kept fresh for every touched callable surface. Drift, growth, and shrink clear only through substantive requirement or scenario edits in the same diff, never through a Spec-Ack trailer.
  - Every conditional clause covered by a test.
- proves: a malformed spec-meta block produces a finding, never a stack trace, on every corpus-reading task.

Allowed touches (this ticket may modify):
- lib/ancora/parser.ex, lib/ancora/index.ex, lib/ancora/verifier.ex, lib/ancora/append_only.ex, lib/ancora/overlap.ex
- lib/ancora/gate.ex, lib/ancora/status.ex, lib/ancora/review.ex, lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex (the four atom-key call sites only)
- lib/ancora/review/html.ex (the fifth accessor variant only)
- lib/ancora/derive/compare.ex (filter non-binary ids only)
- test/ancora/**, test/mix/tasks/**, test/support/**
- .spec/specs/ancora.parsing.spec.md (acknowledgment edits only: substantive requirement/scenario updates that clear drift/growth/shrink for this ticket's own changes; never weakening a must)

- .spec/specs/ancora.derive.spec.md (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator. This list already permits lib/ancora/derive/compare.ex, which ancora.derive governs, so any edit there raises drift that only a substantive edit to this spec can clear. Acknowledgment edits only: substantive requirement or scenario updates that clear drift, growth or shrink caused by THIS ticket's own changes. Never weaken a must, never delete a requirement.)
- .spec/specs/ancora.gate.spec.md (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator. This list already permits lib/ancora/append_only.ex, lib/ancora/change_analysis.ex, lib/ancora/gate.ex, which ancora.gate governs, so any edit there raises drift that only a substantive edit to this spec can clear. Acknowledgment edits only: substantive requirement or scenario updates that clear drift, growth or shrink caused by THIS ticket's own changes. Never weaken a must, never delete a requirement.)

This list already permits lib/ancora/review.ex, lib/ancora/review/html.ex, which ancora.review governs, so any edit there raises drift that only a substantive edit to this spec can clear. Acknowledgment edits only: substantive requirement or scenario updates that clear drift, growth or shrink caused by THIS ticket's own changes. Never weaken a must, never delete a requirement.)
- .spec/specs/ancora.tasks.spec.md (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator. This list already permits lib/ancora/status.ex, which ancora.tasks governs, so any edit there raises drift that only a substantive edit to this spec can clear. Acknowledgment edits only: substantive requirement or scenario updates that clear drift, growth or shrink caused by THIS ticket's own changes. Never weaken a must, never delete a requirement.)
- Any .spec/specs/<subject>.spec.md that `mix spec.check --base <your base>` names in a derived/drift, derived/growth or derived/shrink finding caused by THIS ticket's own diff (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator after the fifth admission defect of this epic. Derivation is file-scoped: every production function called anywhere in a test file joins every subject tagged anywhere in that file, and siblings merging into the epic tip change that set under you, so no list written at admission stays correct. Rule: acknowledgment edits only. Write one substantive requirement or scenario statement describing what THIS ticket changed as THAT subject observes it, verified by execution that the named input actually reaches that subject. Never restate another subject's contract in a second home, never weaken a must, never delete a requirement, never use a Spec-Ack trailer for it. If the subject genuinely observes no change from your work, say so in your completion record and stop; that is an escalation to the orchestrator, not a failure. Every spec edit requires a decision-record edit in the same diff; an affects: entry on your own ADR is the expected form.)
- Any spec whose stated rule THIS ticket's change makes false, for the sole purpose of correcting that statement in the same diff. Recorded after ancora-v1n shipped a corpus holding two scenarios that predicted opposite outcomes from identical input, because the spec stating the old rule was withheld from its Allowed list and the worker retagged around the conflict instead of flagging it. If you find a requirement anywhere in .spec/ that your change falsifies, fixing it here is in scope and expected. Say so in your completion record.

- .spec/decisions/** (added 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator, third instance of the same admission defect, this one found by the ancora-xla.4 verifier. Ancora.PolicyFiles.missing_decision?/1 at lib/ancora/policy_files.ex:115 fires change/missing_decision whenever any path under .spec/specs/ changes without an accompanying decision-record change in the SAME diff. Every ticket here is required to edit a spec, so this finding is structurally guaranteed and the decision-record edit is forced rather than optional. Write a real contract statement describing what you actually built; do NOT add a hollow line to silence the finding, which a grader will read as finding-silencing and bounce.)

- lib/ancora/gate/preflight.ex
- lib/ancora/git*

Out of Scope (intent):

- no env-tier work (ancora-xla.2) and no dead-code sweep (ancora-xla.6)

"invalid spec metadata stays nil and every corpus-reading task handles it" (test/ancora/index_test.exs:141) pins the word "every" against real entry points, not a hand-written list of internal functions. That indirection is forced, not sloppy: spec.next takes no --root and reads File.cwd! at lib/mix/tasks/spec.next.ex:31, so the loop still lands on the same run/1 the mix task invokes. Those six are the complete set of corpus-reading tasks under lib/mix/tasks (the other two are spec.init and spec.decision.new, which write rather than read). The fixture is self-validating: assert spec["meta"] == nil at line 168 fails if the schema ever stops requiring status, so the test cannot silently degrade into asserting on a well-formed spec. It is missing-field malformation rather than type-level, but Zoi collapses both to the same nil-meta path, so a list-where-a-map-belongs fixture would exercise no additional branch. The mutation it kills on the three zero-status tasks is direct: drop the Enum.filter(&is_binary(subject_id(&1))) guard added at lib/ancora/status.ex:138 and Map.fetch!(subject_sets, nil) raises, flipping status away from 0, and refute result.stderr =~ "** (" catches the trace. The check and validate branches assert no stderr cleanliness, but they do not need to: Ancora.Output.gated reraises internal exceptions at lib/ancora/output.ex:66 before render/1 or Verdict.emit run, so a crash produces neither the "spec/parse_error" substring nor the trailing verdict line that List.last(output_lines(...)) demands. Reverting parser.ex:90 to store the raw string-keyed map instead of nil therefore fails these assertions rather than passing on a stack trace. The review leg reads _build/spec_review.html for "spec/parse_error", proving the finding survives all the way to the rendered artifact. UNVERIFIED BY READING: that the verdict line is genuinely the last stdout line under this fixture, and that an injected raise in Ancora.Gate actually reaches the reraise rather than being classified as a usage or env failure. The mutation to run is deleting the is_binary filter at lib/ancora/gate.ex:553 and confirming spec.check stops printing its verdict.

"reads schema structs and YAML maps without creating atoms" (test/ancora/index_test.exs:216) does not count VM atoms, and it does not need to. It brackets the call with assert_raise ArgumentError on String.to_existing_atom of a freshly generated unique name, before and after Index.field/2 sees that name. Reintroducing String.to_atom anywhere on the binary-key path creates the atom and the second assert_raise fails, so the defining phrase "without creating atoms" is pinned by an assertion that a mutation actually breaks. The %{nil => :wrong} argument is the sharper half: it kills the deleted rescue-based shape, which computed a nil atom_key and fell through to Map.get(map, nil), by making that fallback return the sentinel :wrong instead of nil. The struct and string-map assertions cover both arms of Index.field/2 and the nil-meta arm of Index.subject_id/1. Three clauses go uncovered and are worth naming, none blocking: the catch-all field(_value, _key) for a non-map non-nil input, the subject_id(_subject) non-map clause, and the || field(subject, "id") fallback inside subject_id/1, which is unreachable for the real index shape since the key set asserted at line 172 contains no top-level "id". That fallback was inherited verbatim from the four deleted copies. Two further gaps, also non-blocking: the parse_error finding is matched on code only, so a mutation that emptied its detail message survives; and the accessor swaps in verifier.ex, append_only.ex, overlap.ex and review/html.ex are behavior-preserving refactors whose proof rests on existing tagged tests staying green rather than on any changed assertion. No test covers an empty subject id, and I believe it is unreachable because schema validation rejects it before meta is stored, but that reasoning is UNVERIFIED BY READING. The mutation to run is feeding Verifier a subject map with %{"meta" => %{"id" => ""}} and checking whether the invalid-id finding still appears. No existing assertion was deleted or weakened anywhere in the diff; test/ancora/index_test.exs is additions only, and no production function is used to manufacture fixture state.

ADDENDUM to my 02:50:48Z comment. Same verdict, one additional Gap that outranks the one I already filed.
I chased the question the test critic marked UNVERIFIED BY READING at 02:28:56Z, about an empty subject id
reaching invalid_declared_id_findings at base but not at HEAD. The critic guessed the path was unreachable
and so did I in my Notes. We were both wrong, and the reachable version of it is worse than the empty-string
case we were arguing about.

Gap 2 (new, and I would fix this before the one in my first comment):
spec/invalid_id no longer fires for a malformed SUBJECT id, and three false spec/missing_field findings fire
in its place. Fixture: a spec whose spec-meta is `id: Bad Subject!`, `kind: module`, `status: active`, all
three fields present, only the id malformed.
  base 849dbf9, 2 errors, subject column populated with "Bad Subject!":
    spec/parse_error   ... invalid id format: must match "\A[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*\z"
    spec/invalid_id    ... invalid id Bad Subject!; fix the id format
  HEAD d9a39d7, 4 errors, subject column blank:
    spec/parse_error   ... invalid id format: must match "\A[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*\z"
    spec/missing_field ... missing field id; add the required field
    spec/missing_field ... missing field kind; add the required field
    spec/missing_field ... missing field status; add the required field
The author wrote id, kind and status. The tool now tells them all three are missing. Because meta is nil,
Ancora.Verifier.add_missing_fields/6 runs against nil and reports every required key as absent, and
Index.subject_id/1 returns nil so invalid_declared_id_findings skips the subject entirely and every finding
for that file loses its subject attribution.

This is not confined to the exotic case. It is in the ticket's own headline fixture. The spec in
test/ancora/index_test.exs:141 supplies id and kind and omits only status, and HEAD reports missing id,
missing kind and missing status: two of the three lines are false. The test passes because it asserts only
that the stdout contains the string "spec/parse_error", never that the findings describe the file correctly.
Every one of my four malformed fixtures shows the same pattern.

Why this is a Gap and not a Note:
1. It falsifies a must requirement in the spec this diff edits. ancora.parsing.structural_references states
   the parser emits "spec/invalid_id for an id that does not match the dotted-identifier format". At HEAD no
   subject id can ever reach that finding, because any id failing the regex fails schema validation, which
   now nils out meta. I confirmed the requirement/scenario id path is untouched: a fixture with a valid
   subject id and `- id: Bad Req!` produces byte-identical spec/invalid_id output at base and HEAD. It is
   subject ids specifically that lost the finding.
2. The ticket's Allowed touches makes this the implementer's job in this diff, not a follow-up: "Any spec
   whose stated rule THIS ticket's change makes false, for the sole purpose of correcting that statement in
   the same diff ... If you find a requirement anywhere in .spec/ that your change falsifies, fixing it here
   is in scope and expected." The implementer edited that exact requirement and added a sentence to it
   without touching the invalid_id clause it had just made false.
3. It cuts against the ticket's stated purpose. F4's argument is that a user "who made exactly the mistake
   the tool exists to catch" should get the correct finding instead of a stack trace. A malformed subject id
   is exactly that mistake. They no longer get a stack trace, which is the win and it is real, but what they
   get instead is three statements about their file that are not true, with no subject name attached.

What I am not saying: the gate still fails closed on every one of these inputs, 4 errors instead of 2, and
nothing crashes. The parse_error line still names the exact regex, so the information is recoverable. This
is a diagnostic-accuracy regression on the malformed path, not a hole in the gate.

Two shapes of fix, implementer's call:
- Keep the invalid id reachable for reporting. Where schema validation fails on the id format specifically,
  let the subject keep enough identity for invalid_declared_id_findings to fire and for the subject column to
  populate, while still storing nil under "meta" for every reader that expects the validated struct.
- Or suppress the derived missing_field findings when meta is nil, so a nil-meta subject reports the
  parse_error alone rather than inventing three absent fields, and correct the invalid_id clause in
  ancora.parsing.structural_references in the same diff to say what the tool now does.
Either way the regression test at test/ancora/index_test.exs:141 needs an assertion on finding CONTENT, not
just on the "spec/parse_error" substring, or this stays invisible.

Corrections to my first comment:
- The third bullet under Notes, where I argued the empty-string branch of Index.subject_id/1 is unreachable
  and therefore not worth a test, was reasoning rather than execution and it pointed at the wrong question.
  The empty-string literal is indeed rejected upstream, but the branch it feeds, subject_id returning nil for

The failure holds and it is larger than the verifier stated. I also spot-checked two of its claims independently and both are sound, so its re-run evidence is trustworthy. Gap 1 reproduces, and its worst instance is the ticket's own headline fixture, not the exotic one. Running the real mix tasks against a corpus whose spec-meta is `id: broken.subject` / `kind: module` with `status` omitted, the exact fixture at test/ancora/index_test.exs:141: base 849dbf9, 2 errors, subject column `broken.subject`: spec/parse_error ... spec-meta validation failed: is required spec/missing_field ... missing field status HEAD d9a39d7, 4 errors, subject column shows the file path: spec/parse_error ... spec-meta validation failed: is required spec/missing_field ... missing field id spec/missing_field ... missing field kind spec/missing_field ... missing field status The author omitted exactly one field. Base named it. HEAD names three, two of them false, and nothing in HEAD's output identifies `status` as the one that is actually missing: the parse_error message is the bare Zoi string "is required" with no field name, and --verbose is not a valid flag on spec.validate. So the verifier's mitigation "the information is recoverable, the parse_error still names the exact regex" is true only for the malformed-id shape. On the missing-field shape the field name is gone from every channel. That is a straight diagnostic regression on the exact input this ticket exists to serve. The malformed-id shape reproduces as the verifier described. Fixture `id: Bad Subject!` / `kind: module` / `status: active`: base gives spec/parse_error plus spec/invalid_id with the subject column populated; HEAD gives spec/parse_error plus three false spec/missing_field lines and no invalid_id. Mechanism confirmed by reading: Ancora.Schema.Id and Ancora.Verifier use the identical pattern `\A[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*\z`, so any subject id that could fail valid_id?/1 has already failed schema validation, meta is nil, Index.subject_id/1 returns nil, and the `{sid, sid, file}` entry in invalid_declared_id_findings/2 fails its `is_binary(id)` clause. spec/invalid_id is now unreachable for subject ids by construction. Meanwhile add_missing_fields/6 runs Index.field(nil, key) for all three of @meta_required and reports every one absent. That falsifies a must clause in the spec this diff edits. ancora.parsing.structural_references still states the parser emits `spec/invalid_id` for an id that does not match the dotted-identifier format. I confirmed the clause is only false for subjects: a fixture with a valid subject id and `- id: Bad Req!` produces identical spec/parse_error + spec/invalid_id output at base and HEAD. Allowed touches covers the fix twice over, both through the parsing spec itself and through the standing "any spec whose stated rule THIS ticket's change makes false" clause. The verifier is right that this is in scope now, not a follow-up. Gap 2 reproduces. Deleting `|> Enum.filter(&is_binary(subject_id(&1)))` at lib/ancora/review.ex:143 leaves the change-scoped selection green (index, review, review_assets, gate, status: 44 tests, 0 failures) and spec.review against the malformed fixture then emits an empty nav anchor `` and a `
` whose identifier renders as an empty ``. My byte delta is larger than the verifier's 1183 because my fixture had a prior _build/spec_review.html in the diff; the structural change is the same. On the "is it dead code" question: it is not, and it stays under every fix shape on the table. Both of the verifier's proposed remedies leave `"meta" => nil` in place for readers, the outer spec map has no top-level `"id"` key (pinned by the Map.keys assertion at index_test.exs:172), so Index.subject_id/1 still returns nil for a schema-rejected subject and the review view model still sees it. Keep the filter, test it. Spot-checks of the verifier's own evidence, both independent of its re-run: - Mutating Index.field/2's :error branch to `Map.get(map, String.to_atom(key))` fails the trailing assert_raise at index_test.exs:221. CAUGHT, as claimed. - spec.status run from both code versions against one shared well-formed corpus (ancora's own at 849dbf9, via --root) is byte-identical at 530 bytes, matching the verifier's figure exactly. Bounce reason: 1. lib/ancora/verifier.ex plus lib/ancora/parser.ex. A schema-rejected spec-meta now produces spec/missing_field for fields the author wrote, and spec/invalid_id is unreachable for subject ids. Fix, implementer's choice of shape: either suppress the derived spec-meta missing_field findings when meta is nil at add_missing_fields/6 (verifier.ex:53) so the parse_error stands alone, in which case the parse_error detail must be made to name the failing field so `status` does not vanish from the output; or keep the rejected id reachable for reporting so invalid_declared_id_findings/2 and the subject column still see it while `"meta"` stays nil for every reader. Check that proves it: a test running the real mix tasks against two fixtures, one `id: Bad Subject!` with kind and status present, one `id` + `kind` with `status` omitted, asserting the exact set of finding codes and that no spec/missing_field names a field present in the file, and that the output names the field that is genuinely missing. Mutation the check must kill: restoring today's behaviour, deriving missing_field from a nil meta, must fail that test. 2. .spec/specs/ancora.parsing.spec.md, the structural_references invalid_id clause, in the same diff. Whichever shape you pick, the sentence "spec/invalid_id for an id that does not match the dotted-identifier format" must state what the tool does for subject ids, since the requirement/scenario half stays true and only the subject half changed. Every spec edit needs the matching decision-record edit; ancora.decision.invalid_spec_meta already exists and its Decision section is the right home. Check: mix spec.check --base 849dbf9 ends result=pass with no drift, growth or shrink. 3. lib/ancora/review.ex:143. The nil-id filter has no test. Fix: keep the line, add the assertion to the spec.review leg of the test at test/ancora/index_test.exs:141, which already reads _build/spec_review.html back. Refute the empty nav anchor and the empty section id, or assert the rendered subject-section count. Mutation the check must kill: deleting line 143 must fail that test. It survives all 44 change-scoped tests today. 4. test/ancora/index_test.exs:141. `assert check.stdout =~ "spec/parse_error"` is not sufficient for the "finding, not a crash" claim and is the assertion that let items 1 and 3 through. Fix: assert finding content per fixture, the expected code set and the subject attribution, for each malformed shape the test covers. Asserting the exact code for every one of the four shapes the verifier enumerated is not required; asserting content rather than substring presence is. Notes (not blocking): - The verifier described HEAD's subject column as blank. It is blank only on the parse_error line, which renders as `-`. The three missing_field lines carry the file path, because Verifier falls back to `id_of(meta) || file`. The attribution loss is real either way, since base carried the actual subject id. - The verifier's Note calling the empty-string half of Index.subject_id/1 unreachable is correctly superseded by its own addendum. I agree with the supersession and did not re-litigate it. - Its process disclosure checks out on the two claims I could test independently. I raise no evidence-quality objection to the record. - My scratch worktrees were created at unique absolute paths under this session's scratchpad and removed with `git worktree remove --force`. I did not touch scratchpad/mut, scratchpad/base, or /Users/mz/src/ancora, which still sits at d9a39d7 on ancora-gg8/field-friction awaiting the team lead's reset.
